sections.text:
2 Chronicles begins with Solomon and the building of the temple, then follows the kings of Judah alone until the exile. The northern kingdom is mentioned only where it touches Judah’s story.

Again and again the book shows that when a king seeks God, humbles himself and prays, God answers and restores. It ends with the decree of Cyrus of Persia that allows the exiles to go home and rebuild the temple.
The book continues 1 Chronicles and was written after the exile. In the Hebrew Bible, Chronicles stands last, so that the Scriptures end with the invitation to go up to Jerusalem.

The promise of 7:14, that God will hear and heal when his people humble themselves and pray, is often quoted. It was first spoken to Israel about the temple, and Christians differ on how directly to apply it to a modern nation or church. The book’s wider theme is widely shared: it is never too late to turn back to God.
